title: A new limit for an indicator constraint

blocks.text: A district heating model has indicator constraints such as "if boiler $`b`$ runs ($`z_b = 1`$), then $`40 \le \text{heat}_b \le 120`$". Scenario runs need to change a rule's upper limit, and MathOpt cannot edit an indicator constraint (lesson 4.3.1): it has to be deleted and added again.

Write `replace_upper(model, ic, new_upper)`, which replaces the indicator constraint `ic` by one identical in every part except its upper bound, now `new_upper`, and returns the new constraint object. "Every part" is: the indicator variable, the value that switches it on, the lower bound, the variables and coefficients of the row, and the name. The old object must not be used afterwards, which is why the function returns the new one. About eight lines.

Lesson 4.3.1 rebuilds an indicator constraint from its parts: `ic.terms()` gives the row's `(variable, coefficient)` pairs, `mathopt.fast_sum(t.coefficient * t.variable for t in ic.terms())` turns them back into an expression for `implied_expr`, and `implied_lb` and `implied_ub` take the bounds. There is no offset to carry: MathOpt moves a constant in the row into its bounds when it stores the constraint, so the stored expression's constant is 0. Read every part before you delete `ic`.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


def replace_upper(model: mathopt.Model, ic, new_upper: float):
    """Delete `ic` and add the same indicator constraint with upper bound `new_upper`; return the new one."""
    indicator, on_zero, name = ic.indicator_variable, ic.activate_on_zero, ic.name
    lower = ic.lower_bound
    expr = mathopt.fast_sum(term.coefficient * term.variable for term in ic.terms())
    model.delete_indicator_constraint(ic)
    return model.add_indicator_constraint(indicator=indicator, activate_on_zero=on_zero, implied_expr=expr,
                                          implied_lb=lower, implied_ub=new_upper, name=name)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = mathopt.Model()
    z, heat = model.add_binary_variable(name="z"), model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=200, name="heat")
    ic = model.add_indicator_constraint(indicator=z, implied_constraint=(40 <= heat) <= 120, name="boiler")
    print(replace_upper(model, ic, 100).upper_bound)

import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from relimit import replace_upper

# A boiler rule: if run_b2 = 1, then 30 <= heat + 0.25 gas <= 150.
model = mathopt.Model(name="heating")
run = model.add_binary_variable(name="run_b2")
heat = model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=300, name="heat_b2")
gas = model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=400, name="gas_b2")
ic = model.add_indicator_constraint(indicator=run, implied_expr=heat + 0.25 * gas, implied_lb=30,
                                    implied_ub=150, name="boiler_b2")

new = replace_upper(model, ic, 110)
print("new upper limit:", new.upper_bound)
print("new lower limit:", new.lower_bound)
print("new name and indicator:", new.name, new.indicator_variable.name, "on zero", new.activate_on_zero)
print("new terms:", {t.variable.name: t.coefficient for t in new.terms()})
print("indicator constraints in the model:", model.get_num_indicator_constraints())

cases.says: the returned constraint has the new upper bound, the same indicator variable, name and coefficients
the model has the same number of indicator constraints and no longer has the old one
a rule switched on at zero is still switched on at zero after the change
a rule with a lower bound keeps that lower bound after its upper bound changes
